profile.campus: Sterling, Loudoun County, Virginia (QTS Ashburn-Moran campus)
profile.reading:
Per QTS's own site, the Ashburn-Moran facility sits at 44874 Moran Road, Sterling, VA 20166 on a 3-acre campus with 4+ MW critical power capacity, offering N, N+1, and 2N+1 power configuration options with primary and reserved UPS units, primary engine generators, and 48-hour fuel supply.

QTS Data Centers (shown on this row under its pre-2013-IPO name, "Quality Technology Services") was founded in 2003 in Overland Park, Kansas. Per Blackstone's own press release, Blackstone Real Estate Income Trust (BREIT) and other Blackstone-affiliated funds completed a roughly $10 billion acquisition of QTS Realty Trust on August 31, 2021, taking the company private at $78 per share; QTS is no longer an independent SEC filer. QTS's own site lists its US headquarters at 22271 Broderick Drive, Sterling, Virginia, placing this Northern Virginia "Data Center Alley" corridor, alongside neighboring hyperscale and colocation campuses from Amazon, Equinix, Digital Realty, and CyrusOne, at the center of the company's operations.

Dominion Energy, the dominant electric utility across Northern Virginia's data center corridor, has repeatedly cited data center demand growth as a primary driver of its long-term transmission and generation planning, and Loudoun and Prince William County officials have both cited data center real estate and business-license tax revenue as a significant share of their county budgets. QTS's Virginia campuses sit within this same regional grid and policy environment as neighboring hyperscale and colocation buildings operated by Amazon, Equinix, Digital Realty, and CyrusOne, all tracked elsewhere in this registry.

QTS positions itself as a "hyperscale-neutral" wholesale and colocation landlord, leasing built capacity to enterprise, cloud, and hyperscale tenants rather than operating its own end-user cloud service, a business model shared with peers like Digital Realty and CyrusOne in this same Northern Virginia corridor; under Blackstone ownership since 2021, QTS has continued expanding its US footprint (including its Manassas and Richmond 3 campuses, both still under construction as of the facts recorded here) rather than slowing development after going private.

reading.body:
QTS Ashburn-Moran is a 3-acre campus in Sterling, Virginia with 4 MW or more of critical power capacity, configurable across N, N+1, and 2N+1 redundancy tiers with 48-hour fuel backup. The operator does not publish separate figures for IT load versus total facility power, so the precise compute density cannot be stated from the specifications alone. If the 4 MW figure represents IT load at typical AI training density of 40 kW per rack, this would equate to roughly 100 racks, though this is an assumption not confirmed by the published specs.

This campus ranks 24th among the 23 Virginia facilities with published megawatt figures, meaning it falls below the tracked published capacity baseline for the state. Virginia hosts 330 mapped data center facilities and 1,375 MW of published capacity across them, concentrated in Loudoun County's data center corridor where Dominion Energy has identified data center demand as a primary driver of grid planning. QTS operates multiple facilities across this region, positioning Ashburn-Moran as one node in a larger Northern Virginia footprint shared with competing colocation and hyperscale operators.

The campus holds LEED Silver certification, qualifying it for environmentally managed operations. As a wholesale colocation landlord under Blackstone ownership since 2021, QTS markets itself as hyperscale-neutral, meaning the facility's purpose depends on which tenants lease its capacity rather than on QTS operating its own cloud services. The campus sits within the same regional electrical grid and policy environment as neighboring wholesale and hyperscale facilities, subject to the same constraint that grid availability now binds data center scaling across Northern Virginia.
